Name: Christopher Scholes
Details: Christopher Scholes (1819–1894) was an American inventor and businessman, best known for inventing the typewriter. His invention revolutionized communication and document preparation, making it easier for people to create and edit written correspondence.

Name: Grace Hopper
Details: Grace Hopper (1906–1992) was an American computer scientist and United States Navy rear admiral. She was a pioneer in the field of computer programming, developing the first compiler for a computer programming language and popularizing the idea of machine-independent programming languages, which led to the development of COBOL, one of the first high-level programming languages. Hopper's contributions to computing have had a lasting impact on the field.

Name: Alan Turing
Details: Alan Turing (1912–1954) was a British mathematician, logician, and computer scientist who is widely regarded as the father of theoretical computer science and artificial intelligence. He played a pivotal role in breaking the German Enigma code during World War II, significantly contributing to the Allied victory. Turing's groundbreaking work laid the foundation for modern computing, and his legacy continues to influence the field of computer science today.

Name: Ada Lovelace
Details: Ada Lovelace (1815–1852) was an English mathematician and writer, widely recognized as the world's first computer programmer. She is best known for her work on Charles Babbage's early mechanical general-purpose computer, the Analytical Engine. Lovelace's notes on the engine include what is considered the first algorithm intended to be processed by a machine, making her a pioneering figure in the history of computing.

Name: Douglas Englebart
Details: Douglas Engelbart (1925–2013) was an American engineer and computer science pioneer who fundamentally transformed how humans interact with computers. He is globally celebrated for inventing the computer mouse, but his visionary concepts laid the structural groundwork for the entire modern digital age

Name: Founders' Day
Details: Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Day / Founders' Day, celebrated on Monday, September 21, 2026 (formerly known simply as Founders' Day). Ghana also recognizes an alternative Founders' Day on August 4 to honor the 'Big Six' and all patriots who sacrificed for the country's freedom

Name: Tim Berners-Lee
Details: Sir Tim Berners-Lee is the English computer scientist best known as the inventor of the World Wide Web. In 1989, while working as a software engineer at CERN, he proposed a global hypertext project to allow researchers to seamlessly share information. By 1991, he had written the core technologies that still power the modern internet: HTML, HTTP, URLs, the first web browser, and the first web server. Crucially, he chose not to patent his invention, ensuring the Web was released to the public for free, fueling its global, open adoption.
